preconditions.expression: q == int(stdin.split()[0]) and q >= 1 and q <= 150000
preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 150000) representing the number of independent queries.
Each query starts with a line containing an integer n (2 ≤ n ≤ 300000) followed by n-1 lines, each containing two integers x and y (1 ≤ x, y ≤ n) representing edges of a tree.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= int(n) and 1 <= int(y) <= int(n) for n, *edges in (stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)) for x, y in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge (x, y) in the tree connects vertices x and y where 1 ≤ x, y ≤ n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(edge for edges in (stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)) for edge in edges)) == n-1 for n, *edges in (stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)))
preconditions.description: The input graph for each query is a tree (connected and acyclic).

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.splitlines()) == q and stdout.splitlines()[i] == str(max_good_subtree_size) for i, max_good_subtree_size in enumerate(compute_good_subtree_sizes(stdin)))
postconditions.description: For each query, the output is an integer representing the maximum size of a good subtree in the given tree. A good subtree is a connected subgraph that can be represented by segments where edges exist if and only if the corresponding segments intersect.

postconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(output) <= n for output, n in zip(stdout.splitlines(), [int(stdin.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), int(stdin.splitlines()[0])+1)]))
postconditions.description: The output for each query is an integer between 2 and n (inclusive), representing the size of the good subtree.
